newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat meets Israeli defence chief on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets Israeli defence chief on Wednesday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will meet Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Wednesday in the self-ruled Gaza Strip, an adviser to Arafat said on Tuesday.
"President Yasser Arafat is going to meet Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai in Beit Hanoun at 8 p.m. (1700 GMT) tomorrow," adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
Abu Rdainah said Arafat would meet at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT) U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who in Cairo on Tuesday began a drive to revive Middle East peace talks.

Palestinian legislator Hanan Ashrawi said Arafat would demand Mordechai ease the closure of the West Bank and Gaza that prevents Palestinians from working in Israel and carry out the long-delayed redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron.

"The issue of the closure is something that remains on the top of any agenda because it is a form of collective punishment," she told Israel Radio. "The second category has to do with implementation of already agreed upon issues...Among these are the redeployment from Hebron," she said.
In Hebron on Tuesday, Palestinians accused Israel of planning to destroy Arab houses to build a road for Jews.

Hebron is the last of the West Bank Arab cities due to be handed over to self-rule. Under a 1995 peace deal Israel was supposed to hand over parts of the city last March while keeping parts that include the homes of the Jews.

A series of suicide bombings in Israel delayed the handover and the three-month-old right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been demanding changes in the redeployment map it says are necessary to the settlers' safety.

Palestinians view Israeli redeployment in Hebron -- a city of 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jews -- as a litmus test for Israel's commitment to the self-rule deals signed by the Israeli government that Netanyahu ousted in May.
